distillation_scope: Pure disease-name leaf distillation for the full clinical spectrum of visceral leishmaniasis.

latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Reduced or exhausted macrophage/T-cell control that permits Leishmania survival; shaped by age, malnutrition, HIV, transplant or iatrogenic immunosuppression, and parasite-host immune balance.
Intracellular amastigote burden within macrophages of spleen, liver, bone marrow, lymph nodes, and blood mononuclear cells; the core pathogen-load axis reduced by antileishmanial therapy.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Chronic cytokine fever and acute-phase response
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: IL-1, IL-6, TNF, IFN-gamma and macrophage activation causing prolonged or irregular fever, malaise, weight loss, ESR/CRP elevation, hypoalbuminemia, ferritin elevation, and wasting.
Macrophage-rich splenic and hepatic infection causing progressive splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, hypersplenism, cholestatic or mild hepatitic injury, and left upper quadrant fullness.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Bone marrow infection and hematopoietic suppression
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Marrow macrophage infection, inflammatory suppression of hematopoiesis, and hypersplenism producing anemia, leukopenia/neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, and pancytopenia.
Persistent antigenic stimulation causing polyclonal immunoglobulin expansion, hypergammaglobulinemia, high ESR, rouleaux, and plasma-cell-rich marrow findings without monoclonality.

Dysregulated macrophage and T-cell activation triggered by visceral leishmaniasis, producing very high ferritin, cytopenias, hypofibrinogenemia, hypertriglyceridemia, hepatitis, and marrow hemophagocytosis.

Mucosal or extra-reticuloendothelial parasite burden seen especially with HIV or severe immunosuppression, producing esophagitis/gastritis/duodenitis, diarrhea, abdominal pain, pulmonary, renal, skin, or other atypical manifestations.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Persistent parasite reservoir and relapse pathway
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Residual parasite burden after incomplete immune recovery, inadequate drug exposure, prior relapse, or severe immunosuppression; drives recurrent marrow/splenic/GI disease and need for combination or suppressive therapy.
High parasite burden, profound cytopenia, HLH overlap, bacterial coinfection, bleeding, renal injury, or shock physiology causing short-term mortality risk.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Failure of macrophage and T-cell control allows intracellular amastigotes to expand in reticuloendothelial tissue.
Macrophage infection and antigen burden drive chronic inflammatory fever and acute-phase response.
The spleen and liver are major macrophage-rich target organs in visceral leishmaniasis.
Bone marrow macrophage infection and systemic inflammation suppress hematopoiesis and combine with hypersplenism.
Persistent Leishmania antigen stimulation produces polyclonal immunoglobulin expansion.
Leishmania is a recognized infectious trigger of secondary HLH and can be obscured by the HLH phenotype.
Advanced HIV and severe immunosuppression permit atypical mucosal and extra-reticuloendothelial parasite localization.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Amplified by HIV CD4 lymphopenia, absent immune reconstitution, transplant immunosuppression, poor drug exposure, or previous relapse.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Residual parasite reservoirs are the substrate for recurrent VL.
HLH overlap intensifies cytopenias, coagulopathy, hepatic injury, shock risk, and short-term mortality.
Pyrogenic cytokines produce fever that may be irregular, intermittent, or prolonged.
VL often presents as fever of unknown origin with a prolonged fever history.
Untreated VL evolves over weeks to months rather than a single brief febrile episode.
Inflammation, anemia, and wasting produce asthenia and malaise.
Chronic fever and appetite loss cause cachexia and weight loss.
IL-6-driven acute-phase response variably raises CRP.
Inflammation and immunoglobulin expansion commonly produce a high ESR.
Inflammation, malnutrition, and hepatic reprioritization lower albumin.
Splenic macrophage infection and congestion produce the classic enlarged spleen.
Measured splenic length captures the same splenic involvement without forcing a qualitative score.
Hepatic reticuloendothelial infection can enlarge the liver.
Hepatic involvement and HLH overlap can cause mild-to-moderate transaminitis.
VL may produce mild cholestatic liver test abnormalities.
Marrow suppression, inflammation, and hypersplenism lower hemoglobin.
Leukopenia is a common component of VL pancytopenia.
Neutropenia reflects marrow suppression and hypersplenism.
Thrombocytopenia arises from hypersplenism, marrow suppression, and HLH overlap.
Polyclonal immunoglobulin expansion is characteristic and can mimic plasma-cell or autoimmune disease.
Hypergammaglobulinemia may offset hypoalbuminemia and keep total protein normal or elevated.
Macrophage activation can raise ferritin into HLH-like ranges.
HLH physiology impairs lipid handling and raises triglycerides.
HLH consumptive/inflammatory coagulopathy can lower fibrinogen.
The combined syndrome can satisfy HLH criteria and needs trigger-directed treatment.
Gastrointestinal mucosal leishmaniasis may cause abdominal pain or fullness.
GI involvement in HIV-associated VL can cause intermittent diarrhea.
Upper GI involvement or drug toxicity can produce nausea and vomiting.
Persistent parasite burden under poor cellular immunity produces recurrent VL.
Severe infection, dehydration, amphotericin exposure, and sepsis can precipitate AKI.
Severe thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, and marrow failure increase bleeding risk.
Mortality emerges from untreated parasite burden, HLH overlap, profound cytopenia, coinfection, renal injury, and shock physiology.

Neutropenia often tracks marrow and splenic involvement.

Multilineage cytopenia pattern; individual CBC axes remain primary measurements.

Hazard of secondary HLH/MAS phenotype triggered by VL.
Bleeding hazard rises with severe thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, or invasive procedures.
AKI hazard reflects severe illness and amphotericin toxicity context.
Bacterial sepsis risk from neutropenia, frailty, hospitalization, urinary infection, or AIDS.
Post-treatment relapse hazard, especially in HIV or persistent immunosuppression.
Probability that the selected regimen is active, deliverable, absorbed, and dosed adequately for the parasite and host context.
Advanced HIV, poor immune reconstitution, or very low CD4 count.

Renal reserve, dehydration, nephrotoxins, and amphotericin formulation context.

Confirmatory parasite visualization in bone marrow, splenic aspirate, liver, lymph node, blood, or tissue; not ordinary presentation evidence.
Confirmatory molecular evidence; useful for relapse monitoring in immunosuppressed hosts.
rK39, DAT, immunochromatography, IFAT, ELISA, or other Leishmania serology; sensitivity reduced in HIV and does not distinguish cure from past exposure reliably.
Lifespan outcome hazard emerging from untreated burden, HLH overlap, bacterial sepsis, bleeding, renal injury, frailty, and relapse.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Hypersplenism and splenic sequestration contribute to thrombocytopenia.
Hypersplenism can lower leukocyte count in parallel with marrow suppression.
Anemia worsens fatigue and weakness beyond cytokine effects.
Globulin expansion and fibrinogen elevate ESR.
Severe thrombocytopenia increases clinically important bleeding risk.

axis_couplings.conditionality: Most informative when accompanied by cytopenias, fever, hypofibrinogenemia, or hypertriglyceridemia.
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: High ferritin is a key HLH-pattern signal but is interpreted with the whole inflammatory pattern.
Hypertriglyceridemia supports transition toward HLH phenotype.
Hypofibrinogenemia is an HLH criterion and indicates consumptive inflammatory coagulopathy.
HLH overlap increases mortality through hyperinflammation, cytopenia, coagulopathy, and organ dysfunction.
Major bleeding events reduce survival in severe cytopenic VL.
Bacterial sepsis can dominate short-term mortality in frail or neutropenic VL.
Recurrent untreated or refractory VL increases cumulative mortality risk.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Adequate dosing and delivery are required for parasite clearance.
Renal toxicity risk requires hydration and electrolyte monitoring but does not remove direct antileishmanial activity.
HIV-associated VL has higher initial failure and relapse despite active induction therapy.

failure_modes: renal toxicity or electrolyte wasting limiting treatment

side_effects.interpretation: Amphotericin exposure can increase AKI hazard, lower with liposomal formulation and monitoring.
Creatinine rise may occur during therapy.

treatments.context_specific_role: High-potency induction and pregnancy-compatible option; relapse prevention still depends on immune recovery and adequate total exposure.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Deoxycholate amphotericin has greater nephrotoxicity and infusion toxicity than liposomal formulation.

failure_modes: insufficient total exposure in severe or HIV-associated disease
treatments.context_specific_role: Active alternative when liposomal formulation is not available or affordable, with higher toxicity burden.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Miltefosine is teratogenic and requires pregnancy avoidance.
Miltefosine can add an independent antileishmanial mechanism in HIV relapse regimens.

failure_modes: pregnancy or inability to ensure contraception

side_effects.interpretation: Renal toxicity or monitoring issue is possible but usually less central than amphotericin.

treatments.context_specific_role: Oral option and useful component of relapse or HIV-associated combination therapy when pregnancy is excluded.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Paromomycin effectiveness is regimen- and region-dependent.

failure_modes: insufficient activity as a single agent in some contexts
treatments.context_specific_role: Injectable component in validated regional regimens or combination strategies.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: HIV coinfection is associated with higher toxicity and poorer outcomes with antimonials.
Resistance and regional efficacy constraints can make antimonials ineffective.

side_effects.interpretation: Severe antimonial toxicity can add hazard through arrhythmia, pancreatitis, or organ injury.

treatments.context_specific_role: Region-dependent option whose usefulness is strongly constrained by resistance and toxicity context.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Combination therapy addresses high failure and relapse risk in advanced HIV.
Prior relapse signals persistent reservoir and need for greater antileishmanial pressure.

failure_modes: drug interactions or intolerance prevent combination
parasite persists in marrow, spleen, or GI tissue

side_effects.interpretation: Oral components can add GI intolerance.
Polyene or aminoglycoside components can add renal risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Escalated antileishmanial pressure for relapse, HIV-associated VL, or high failure-risk contexts.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Relapse prevention depends heavily on cellular immune recovery.

failure_modes: poor monitoring for PCR or symptoms

side_effects.interpretation: Intermittent polyene suppression can still carry renal/electrolyte toxicity.

treatments.context_specific_role: Maintenance or close molecular monitoring strategy when relapse risk remains high after apparent response.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Immune reconstitution reduces persistence and relapse risk, although it is slower than direct antileishmanial therapy.

failure_modes: poor CD4 recovery despite virologic suppression
late initiation after severe VL organ injury
treatments.context_specific_role: Host-state repair for HIV-associated VL; does not replace immediate antileishmanial therapy.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Reducing permissive immunosuppression helps clear intracellular parasites when clinically feasible.

failure_modes: rejection risk or autoimmune flare prevents reduction
reduction too small to restore cellular control

side_effects.interpretation: Rejection or inflammatory flare can add hazard outside direct VL control.

treatments.context_specific_role: Adjunctive host-control maneuver in transplant, biologic, steroid, or cytotoxic immunosuppression contexts.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Direct hyperinflammation control may be needed when HLH physiology is life-threatening.
Immunosuppression without parasite control can worsen the hidden infectious trigger.

failure_modes: leishmaniasis not recognized and trigger-directed therapy delayed
underlying malignancy or alternative HLH trigger missed

side_effects.interpretation: Corticosteroid or HLH therapy can further impair parasite control.
Additional immune suppression can increase bacterial infection risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Conditional bridge for life-threatening HLH physiology, paired with active antileishmanial therapy.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: VL is geographically clustered by vector and reservoir exposure.

cd4_below_200_or_discordant_cd4_recovery.trajectory_modulation: More atypical GI disease, weaker serology, higher parasite burden, treatment failure, and relapse.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: CD4 lymphopenia is central to HIV-associated VL persistence.
Atypical mucosal and disseminated tissue disease is enriched in HIV coinfection.
VL-HIV coinfection has high relapse risk when CD4 recovery remains poor.

treatment_effect_modulation.combination_antileishmanial_therapy_for_: often becomes more useful as relapse/failure risk rises
treatment_effect_modulation.antiretroviral_therapy_optimization_in_h: reduces long-run persistence and relapse but acts slowly

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises parasite burden, atypical presentation, relapse, and competing treatment toxicity constraints.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Iatrogenic immune suppression permits intracellular parasite persistence.
Cell-mediated immune control is impaired.
Persistent immunosuppression makes eradication harder.

treatment_effect_modulation.reduce_iatrogenic_immunosuppression_when: can strengthen host control but must be balanced against rejection or inflammatory flare

present.trajectory_modulation: Shifts current syndrome toward relapse or persistent reservoir when compatible cytopenia/splenomegaly returns.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Previous relapse signals parasite persistence or inadequate immune control.
Prior relapse is a strong future-relapse context.

present.trajectory_modulation: Increases progression, cytopenia severity, secondary infection, and mortality tolerance cost.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Malnutrition and frailty lower albumin independent of active parasite burden.
Poor reserve and cytopenia increase bacterial complication risk.

present.trajectory_modulation: Prolongs fever, worsens splenic/marrow disease, and increases relapse or severe organ dysfunction.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Delayed diagnosis allows the FUO phenotype to persist.
Untreated parasite burden accumulates in macrophage-rich organs.
Inadequate exposure leaves persistent reservoirs.

present_or_high_probability.trajectory_modulation: Does not make VL an HLH subtype; it intensifies ferritin, cytopenias, coagulopathy, hepatic injury, and mortality.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: VL-triggered HLH is a severe expression of the same infection.
HLH overlap can push ferritin much higher than uncomplicated VL.
Hypofibrinogenemia supports HLH physiology.
Hyperinflammation and organ dysfunction raise short-term mortality.

present.trajectory_modulation: Mainly shifts creatinine background and amphotericin toxicity hazard rather than VL likelihood.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Baseline renal disease raises creatinine independent of VL.
Renal impairment and nephrotoxins amplify amphotericin toxicity risk.

present.trajectory_modulation: Changes drug feasibility and raises maternal-fetal management complexity outside the current lifespan-only outcome.

axis_response_modulation.clinical_rationale: Pregnancy is a core treatment-context modifier for antileishmanial choices.

supportive_care: Keep parasite-confirming tests out of ordinary ranking evidence: bone marrow or splenic aspirate microscopy, tissue pathology, PCR, culture, and serology belong in confirmatory/pathology/microbiology context.

Assess the core presentation axes early: fever duration, spleen size, CBC with differential, albumin, liver tests, ESR/CRP, ferritin, triglycerides, fibrinogen, creatinine, and bleeding or infection complications.
When splenic aspirate is considered, balance diagnostic yield against bleeding risk from thrombocytopenia and splenomegaly.
Screen for HLH overlap when fever, cytopenias, high ferritin, hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia, hepatitis, encephalopathy, or marrow hemophagocytosis are present.
In HIV-associated VL, document CD4 count, viral load, antiretroviral history, prior VL episodes, GI symptoms, marrow or tissue disease, and relapse monitoring plan.
In transplant or immunosuppressed patients, coordinate antileishmanial therapy with transplant/rheumatology/oncology teams before reducing immunosuppression.
During amphotericin therapy, monitor creatinine, potassium, magnesium, volume status, infusion reactions, anemia, and concomitant nephrotoxins.
Treat or prevent secondary bacterial infection when neutropenia, urinary infection, catheter exposure, hospitalization, or shock physiology appears.
Use transfusion, bleeding precautions, nutrition support, fever control, hydration, and ICU support as dictated by the observed axes rather than as diagnosis labels.
After apparent response, monitor for relapse clinically and, where available, by PCR or tissue/marrow reassessment in high-risk HIV or immunosuppressed patients.
quality_notes: No treatment ranking-label fields are used.
Treatment trajectory_modifications are dictionaries keyed by latent mechanism or axis id.
Confirmatory microbiology and pathology axes are defined for ontology completeness; case files should put these evidence types outside ordinary observations with use_in_ranking:false.
